_note: THIS factory's board-intake exemptions, read by tests/test_board_intake_recorded.py. ONE entry, admitted because NO TRUTHFUL VALUE RESTORES THE SCOPE. The row is LAWFUL: n=5067 records #857, filed on the fork leshchenko1979/opencrabs under the two-stream routing law, and it is a true record of a fork filing. What the reverse arm could not see is that the number belongs to ANOTHER board: `intaken_numbers` resolves a bare `#NNN` subject against THIS board only, so it read #857 as a number that exists nowhere. The predicate now reads `refs` (#647 half 1), but this row declares `refs=[{"board": "857"}]` — a board ref with no repo qualifier — so there is nothing for half 1 to read. Its refs are PUBLISHED and immutable (docs/instruments/ledger.md §9.1), and a `repo` ref appended after the fact would record a declaration that was never made: the no-backfill family (§9.12), a falsified record rather than a repair. The bar is therefore TRUTHFULNESS, not reach, and `bar=no-truthful-value` is the one lawful value. It is printed as an 'excused:' line with its reason and proof on EVERY gate run, so it is a visible debt rather than forgiveness. THE REMEDY IS THE WRITER RULE, not a second entry: every cross-repo intake row from here carries a `repo` ref naming the other repository, so half 1 sees it and no exemption is needed. That rule is UNENFORCED BY CONSTRUCTION — the omission is indistinguishable at the bytes from an ordinary in-repo intake row, so no gate can uphold it — and it is stated rather than implied. Skeleton and field rules: docs/board-intake-exemptions.example.json.

exemptions.domain: the intake row names an issue on another repository and declares no repo ref
exemptions.reason: The intake row n=5067 records #857, filed on the fork leshchenko1979/opencrabs under the two-stream routing law, and its refs are [{"board": "857"}] — a board ref with NO repo qualifier. The reverse arm resolves a bare `#NNN` subject against THIS board only, so it read #857 as a number this board never had: a permanent red no writer can clear, because the row is published and its refs are immutable (§9.1). Half 1 of #647's remedy (the predicate reads `refs`) cannot reach it, because the row declares no `repo` ref to read. Backfilling one is BARRED and the bar is not a formality: a ref appended after the fact records a declaration that was never made, which is the no-backfill family (§9.12) — a falsified record, not a repair. HQ ruled the row LAWFUL and ordered this exemption as the honest exit (ruling n=5105). It is LOUD: the leg prints it by row number and repository, so it can never be mistaken for a clean row.
exemptions.proof: `gh issue view 857 --repo leshchenko1979/opencrabs --json state,number,url` reads state=OPEN, number=857, url=https://github.com/leshchenko1979/opencrabs/issues/857 — the issue is REAL and OPEN on the other repository, so the intake row is a true record. `gh issue view 857 --json state` on this board returns `GraphQL: Could not resolve to an issue or pull request with the number of 857.` — the same number resolves to nothing HERE, which is exactly why the reverse arm fired. Both reads taken 2026-11-16 against the live board and the live fork.
